conventions.commits: Conventional Commits (type(scope): subject, e.g. 'feat(core): add Swift language support with tree-sitter-swift handler (#1742)'); every commit needs Signed-off-by (DCO) and GPG signing (git commit -S --signoff per CONTRIBUTING.md). In this clone the HEAD commit reports GPG status E (signature present, not verifiable locally).
conventions.testing: Unit tests live in #[cfg(test)] mod tests at the bottom of each languages/<lang>.rs file (queries_compile, element query happy path, inheritance, defuse write site); registry tests live in languages/mod.rs and lang.rs; integration tests live in crates/aptu-coder/tests/ (shared harness in tests/common/mod.rs) and crates/aptu-coder-core/tests/. Run with cargo test.
conventions.linting: cargo fmt --check; cargo clippy --locked --profile ci -- -D warnings -W clippy::cognitive_complexity (CI Lint job on ubuntu-26.04-arm); workspace lints deny undocumented_unsafe_blocks, unwrap_used, expect_used (test code exempt via cfg_attr in lib.rs); SPDX header check in CI; cargo deny check advisories licenses bans; REUSE compliance; Cargo.lock new entries must be >= 7 days old (SKIP_PACKAGE_AGE_CHECK bypass exists but the issue forbids using it).
conventions.error_handling: Handlers return Option<String> / Vec<String> and never panic; get_node_text() bounds-checks byte ranges and returns None on overflow; query compile failures surface as ParserError::QueryError from parser.rs; library errors use thiserror; test code uses expect("...") with messages.

patterns: Registry pattern: each language module exports const query strings (ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, DEFUSE_QUERY) and optional handlers; languages/mod.rs wires them into a LanguageInfo arm in get_language_info() and a grammar arm in get_ts_language().

Capture-name contract: extract_elements only reads captures named function, func_name, method_name, class, class_name, type_name; calls read 'call'; imports read 'import_path'; def-use reads write.* / read.* / writeread.* prefixes. New queries must use these exact names.

Java template: ELEMENT_QUERY pairs each declaration node with a name capture and an @function or @class outer capture; extract_inheritance walks named fields (superclass, interfaces). PHP cannot copy the field walk because base_clause and class_interface_clause are unnamed children.

Swift template: extract_inheritance iterates node.child(i) and matches child.kind() (inheritance_specifier), which is the pattern PHP needs; it returns 'extends X' for the first entry and 'conforms X' after that.

Java DEFUSE_QUERY: write captures (write.local, write.assign), a writeread capture (writeread.update) and a catch-all read capture (read.usage); extract_def_use de-duplicates reads that share a byte offset with a write.

CSS wiring: the css module is registered in the workspace and crate Cargo.toml, EXTENSION_MAP, pub mod, get_language_info, get_ts_language and the table-driven test; it is absent from supported_languages().

Import fallback: IMPORT_QUERY capture with no dedicated arm in extract_imports_from_node results in ImportInfo.module equal to the full trimmed node text (the _ arm), which is how Java import_declaration works today.
enclosing_function_name() already handles function_definition and method_declaration kinds by name field, so call-site caller attribution needs no core changes for PHP.

approaches.name: A: Java/Swift-template full handler with LANGUAGE_PHP (recommended)
approaches.description: Add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to root and core Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock; create languages/php.rs with ELEMENT_QUERY (function_definition, method_declaration, class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration), CALL_QUERY (function_call_expression, member_call_expression, nullsafe_member_call_expression, scoped_call_expression), REFERENCE_QUERY (named_type name), IMPORT_QUERY (namespace_use_declaration, relying on the raw-text fallback), DEFUSE_QUERY (assignment, augmented assignment, update, simple_parameter, static_variable_declaration, global_declaration, variable_name reads), and extract_inheritance that walks base_clause and class_interface_clause children by kind(). Wire "php" into lang.rs EXTENSION_MAP, supported_languages(), languages/mod.rs (pub mod, get_language_info with LANGUAGE_PHP, get_ts_language), add the registry table row and a README update.
pros: Matches every acceptance criterion in #1864 with the same file set and shape as Java and Swift
No change to shared core code; all PHP behaviour lives in languages/php.rs
The DEFUSE_QUERY slot is filled so the defuse compile path in parser.rs and the extract_def_use tests cover PHP
Uses only node kinds and fields confirmed in node-types.json and upstream tags.scm
cons: Import records carry the full statement text (for example 'use App\\Models\\User;') as module, the same limitation Java has today
Query text is unverified until a unit test compiles it; a wrong capture name fails silently in extract_elements
Needs an HTML-template test to prove LANGUAGE_PHP yields zero ERROR nodes for mixed files

approaches.name: B: Minimal element, call and import handler
approaches.description: Same registry wiring as A, but languages/php.rs holds only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY and IMPORT_QUERY, with REFERENCE_QUERY and DEFUSE_QUERY set to None and extract_inheritance set to None in LanguageInfo.
pros: Smallest diff, with the fewest queries to validate
Gets PHP into the analyze_file and analyze_directory output quickly
cons: Fails the issue's inheritance acceptance criteria (extends and implements) and the five-query scope
defuse_query None makes extract_def_use return an empty list for PHP
Leaves a known gap that a follow-up issue would have to close

approaches.name: C: A plus a structural namespace_use_declaration arm in the shared import extractor
approaches.description: Do approach A and additionally add a 'namespace_use_declaration' arm to extract_imports_from_node in parser_elements.rs that splits 'use A\\B\\C as D;' into module 'A\\B' and items ['C'] (aliases via namespace_use_clause alias field, group use via namespace_use_group).
pros: Import shape matches Rust and Python (module plus items) rather than raw statement text
Makes PHP imports usable by consumers that compare module and item names
cons: Touches shared core code (parser_elements.rs), which the issue does not ask for and may count as scope creep under the maintainers' rules
Adds about 9 files and a second test surface; the arm must be guarded to avoid changing other languages' output
Not required by any acceptance criterion in #1864

recommendation: Approach A. It meets every acceptance criterion in #1864, follows the Java and Swift registry shape the issue names, keeps all PHP logic in languages/php.rs, and leaves shared core code untouched. Use LANGUAGE_PHP (not LANGUAGE_PHP_ONLY) so the HTML-template criterion can pass. Defer the structured import arm of approach C to a follow-up, since the issue does not require it. Verify every query by compiling it in the unit test before wiring the registry, as the issue's step 3 suggests.
element_query_draft:
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
inheritance_walk_citation: Grammar source inspected: tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php php/src/node-types.json (fetched via gh api; php/grammar.js is only `const defineGrammar = require('../common/define-grammar.js'); module.exports = defineGrammar('php');`, and the rules live in common/define-grammar.js, which was not walked in full). Field-by-field walk from a class_declaration node: (1) class_declaration has field 'name' (required, type 'name') and field 'body' (required, type 'declaration_list'); there is no field named 'superclass' or 'interfaces', so Java's child_by_field_name approach returns None. (2) The extends list is in an UNNAMED CHILD of kind 'base_clause' (multiple, required, children types 'name' | 'qualified_name' | 'relative_name'): iterate node.child(i), match kind() == "base_clause", then iterate its named children of those kinds and emit "extends <text>". (3) The implements list is in UNNAMED CHILD(ren) of kind 'class_interface_clause' (multiple, required, children 'name' | 'qualified_name' | 'relative_name'): same walk, emit "implements <text>". Upstream queries/tags.scm confirms this shape: `(class_interface_clause [(name) (qualified_name)] @name) @reference.implementation`. Interface declarations use base_clause for their extends list; enum_declaration uses class_interface_clause for implements and primitive_type for the backing type. Expected result for `class Foo extends Bar implements A, B {}`: ["extends Bar", "implements A", "implements B"]; for `class Plain {}`: [].
